title: Ariadne Loop project quality
goal: Improve Ariadne Loop into a high-quality public project without broad churn, stale outputs, or unverifiable claims
current_state: The project has a Python CLI, loop builder core, GitHub Pages docs, bilingual homepage and builder pages, generated examples, schemas, and pytest coverage. Recent homepage and builder copy changes are live on GitHub Pages. Each new optimization turn must start from the current repository state, not memory.
recent_progress: Homepage and builder copy were tightened
GitHub Pages was verified after recent updates
The project has CLI, docs, generated examples, and report supervision flows
The current automated baseline is python -m pytest -q
constraints: Read current files, tests, docs, CLI behavior, and git state before changing anything
Prefer small reviewable improvements over broad rewrites
Do not change public CLI commands, JSON schema, package metadata, or published URLs without tests and docs
Keep generated examples in sync with the current CLI output
Preserve bilingual public pages; run the CJK output quality gate when touching Chinese HTML or docs
Do not invent quality claims without evidence from tests, browser checks, file readback, or remote readback
Do not tag, release, publish packages, or make external-impact changes without human confirmation
verifiers: Generated examples that were touched are regenerated by the current CLI and validate
If public HTML changes, desktop and mobile browser checks show no text overflow, clipped controls, or broken language switching
If Chinese public content changes, output_quality_gate.py passes with --expect-cjk
README, docs, and Pages links point to existing files or live URLs
git diff contains only changes needed for the selected quality improvement
open_questions: Which quality area has the highest leverage this turn: project structure, CLI output, generated examples, docs, tests, or release hygiene?
Is the next change meant to be local-only, committed, or pushed to the public repository?
